## What to do, and how long it takes

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| **1** | Read Valeriano & Maness (selected chapters) and Farrell & Newman | 75 min |
| **2** | Download DCID v2.0 and EuRepoC v1.3 | 15 min |
| **3** | **Submit the GSDB request form** | 5 min |
| **4** | Self-check | 15 min |

## 1 · Read

**Valeriano & Maness (2015), *Cyber War versus Cyber Realities*, Oxford UP**

::: {.muted}
[doi:10.1093/acprof:oso/9780190204792.001.0001](https://doi.org/10.1093/acprof:oso/9780190204792.001.0001) · introduction, the theory of restraint, the data chapter
:::

**Farrell & Newman (2019), *Weaponized Interdependence*, International Security 44(1): 42–79**

::: {.muted}
[doi:10.1162/isec_a_00351](https://doi.org/10.1162/isec_a_00351) · in full — it returns in Sessions 10 and 11
:::

| | Annotate |
|---|---|
| **1** | Who targets whom, how severely, and why |
| **2** | How the incident data are built |
| **3** | Panopticon vs chokepoint |
| **4** | Why a firm with no quarrel might be hit |

## 2 · Get the data

::: {.step}
**DCID v2.0** — Dataverse [doi:10.7910/DVN/CQOMYV](https://doi.org/10.7910/DVN/CQOMYV) → *Access File → CSV (original)* · codebook 2.0 on [ryanmaness.com](https://www.ryanmaness.com/cyber-conflict-dataset)
:::

::: {.step}
**EuRepoC v1.3** — Zenodo [doi:10.5281/zenodo.14965395](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.14965395) → `eurepoc_global_dataset_1_3.csv` + `eurepoc_codebook_1_2.pdf`
:::

```text
08-cyber-geopolitics/data/raw/
```

In the DCID codebook, find: the **unit**, the list of **methods**, the **severity** scale.

## 3 · Request the GSDB — now

::: {.warn}
Session 10 needs the **Global Sanctions Data Base**. It is free, but sent **on request**, by e-mail.
:::

::: {.step}
[globalsanctionsdatabase.com](https://globalsanctionsdatabase.com/) → request form → HEC address → "academic use, INTE 60019A"
:::

::: {.muted}
No redistribution, no commercial use: the file stays on your machine; workbooks go to ZoneCours only.
:::

## 4 · Self-check

1. **Restraint** by whom — and why hold back a weapon you have?
2. **Panopticon** vs **chokepoint**: one example each involving a private firm
3. Why is **attribution** a problem for whoever builds the dataset?
4. Name a multinational hit by an operation **not aimed at it**

## Arrive with

::: {.check}
- Both readings annotated
- DCID and EuRepoC in `data/raw/`, with codebooks
- **GSDB request submitted**
- Your self-check, on paper
:::
